newsitem.title: GHANA: Tremor shakes part of Ghana capital.
newsitem.headline: Tremor shakes part of Ghana capital.

text.p: An earth tremor measuring 4.5 on the open-ended Richter scale shook a district of Ghana's capital Accra on Wednesday, the director of the Geological Survey Department said.
Charles Oduro told Reuters the five-minute early-morning tremor shook buildings in Weija, a suburb of Accra-West. A smaller after-shock was registered around noon.
"If some windows of buildings in Weija were shattered, that is because these buidings were poorly constructed," Oduro said.
The tremor was the strongest since 1969 when one of similar magnitude was recorded by the Geological Survey Department.
In 1939 an earthquake estimated by some of 6.5, by others of 8.0 on Richter scale, killed 16 people and injured 133 in Accra.
Accra is on a junction of two major and two minor fault lines.

"The occurance of the 1939 earthquake and recent micro-seismic activities indicate that the occurance of another major earthquake should not be ruled out," a recent seismological report from the Geological Survey Department said.
